ca_hogwild.blurb: Hogwild is the far western end of the Hogsback, the lower formation in front of Lover's Leap on the Highway 50 corridor near Lake Tahoe. It holds 26 routes, almost all of them trad, plus a pair of bolted lines. The grades start easy and climb gradually, with a good share of 5.6 to 5.9 leads and only a few 5.10s and a single 5.11. Several routes run to three or even five pitches, yet the setting is gentler and less exposed than the big cliff behind it, which makes it a friendly place for newer trad leaders. Most lines face north and west, so the afternoon brings the sun.
ca_hogwild.approach: A short wooded trail leads in from the campground to the base of the crag.

ca_hillis_beach.blurb: Hillis Beach is a bouldering area on the Madera side of Millerton Lake, in the Sierra foothills northeast of Fresno. Granite boulders sit scattered along a sandy shoreline at low elevation, and you can wander between most of the 26 problems on foot from either of the two parking areas. The grades lean easy: a lot of V0 and V1, a handful of V2 and V3, and a few harder lines up to V6, so it suits beginners and anyone wanting a relaxed session. Landings can be sandy, and broken glass and rattlesnakes are worth watching for around the base of the rocks.

ca_west_face_6.blurb: The West Face is part of Sugarloaf, a granite formation along Highway 50 near Strawberry and Kyburz, west of Lover's Leap in the Lake Tahoe region. It carries 26 routes, mostly hard bolted faces with a smaller set of trad lines. The grades are steep for a crag this size: a few 5.8s and 5.9s, then a big cluster of 5.10 and 5.11, finishing with a handful of 5.12s and one 5.13. As the name suggests, the wall faces west and gets the afternoon sun, while trees keep a few of the lower single-pitch lines in shade. Summer runs hot here, so spring and fall tend to be the comfortable seasons.

_expect.name: Left Hand of Darkness - E. Face

ca_left_hand_of_darkness_e_face.blurb: The east face of Left Hand of Darkness is a roadside wall in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park, a few minutes from the pavement where the main park road meets Lost Horse Road. Its 26 routes are mostly crack and face trad, with several top-rope options. Grades run from 5.5 up to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range and a good number of 5.10s. Because the face looks east, it stays in shade through the afternoon and gets very little winter sun, so it is best for warm days. Some lines have spaced protection, so bring a full rack.
